title: Maximum k-cut with variational quantum circuits

problem.name: Maximum k-cut
problem.statement_latex:
Given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$, nonnegative rational edge weights $w_{uv}$ and an integer $k\ge3$, find $c:V\to\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ maximizing
\[
C(c)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E}w_{uv}\,\mathbf1[c(u)\ne c(v)].
\]
The approximation version requests a labeling with a specified value relative to the optimum or total edge weight. Write $n=|V|$ and $m=|E|$. The problem models partitioning into several groups and extends the binary cut objective. Complexity counts quantum gates and measurement samples, classical arithmetic for approximation, and bit operations for exact finite-precision optimization.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(KSpk(m+n))$ gates, one-hot QAOA with a parity-ring mixer; polynomial-size qudit QAOA with a Grover mixer.
quantum.details_latex: Here $p$ is the number of alternating layers, $K$ counts evaluated parameter settings and $S$ is the number of samples per setting. The one-hot encoding uses $nk$ data qubits; its cost layer has $O(km)$ two-qubit phases and its mixer has $O(kn)$ two-qubit rotations. Each sample is a classical $k$-labeling. Binary encodings use $n\lceil\log_2k\rceil$ data qubits and additional gates for unused labels. The classical parameter optimization and gate-synthesis precision contribute to total cost. For the qudit Grover-mixer algorithm on unweighted $d$-regular graphs of girth $g\ge2p+2$, Apte et al. compute the expected cut fraction and identify $k=3,4$ comparisons in which depths starting at $p=9$ exceed the analyzed classical Local Vector guarantees. Their expectation calculation costs $O(pk^{2(p+1)})$ classical time and $O(k^{2p})$ memory, with $d$ entering the numerical values.

classical.headline_latex: Polynomial time, Frieze--Jerrum approximation and the Local Vector algorithm; $\operatorname{poly}(n,m,W)k^{\omega n/3}$ for exact integer-weighted 2-CSP.
classical.details_latex: Frieze--Jerrum rounding gives approximation ratio $\alpha_k$, with $\alpha_3\simeq0.836008$ and $\alpha_k=1-1/k+(2+o(1))\log(k)/k^2$. Garc\'ia-Soriano and Miyauchi give certified ratios for $3\le k\le16$ and characterize the ratio for every $k\ge3$. On regular graphs with a girth promise, the Local Vector algorithm supplies the cut-fraction comparison. For exact optimization, $\omega$ is the matrix-multiplication exponent and $W$ bounds the scaled integer score. A threshold circuit with $L$ gates gives $\operatorname{poly}(L)2^{O(L/\sqrt{\log L})}$ time through exact 3-CNF counting; enumeration gives $O^*(k^n)$. The smallest applicable bound is used. At fixed $k$, unit weights and $m=O(n)$, threshold counting gives $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$.
